ship.lore: The Cthulhu is a class of dreadnought constructed by the Scourge. Alongside its sister class, the Nosferatu, the Cthulhu is one of the largest armed vessels brought to bear by the Scourge, dwarfed only by the rarely-seen super-dreadnoughts. As with the Nosferatu, the Cthulhu is equipped with banks of Oculus weaponry, launch capacity to rival that of a fleet carrier, and cloaking capabilities to let it reach optimal firing position. However, the Cthulhu is also armed with one of the most fearsome weapons a commander could face in void combat: the furnace triad. This triple-barreled furnace cannon array is capable of bisecting a battleship in a single discharge, destroying enemy capital ships in an instant. Though the destructive applications of this are immediately evident, the effect on morale is perhaps more insidious, few captains have survived an encounter with a Cthulhu and lived to pass on their experience, which means other commanders tend to panic when one uncloaks. The fixed position of the furnace triad is the only saving grace for those who face a Cthulhu, as it can potentially be outmanoeuvred and deprived of its biggest weapon.

ship.lore:
The Lucifer is a class of battleship designed and constructed by the Scourge. Alongside two other battleship classes, Lucifers have begun appearing over contested Cradle Worlds and have been sighted in the Solar system, reinforcing existing Scourge assets in these theaters. Similarly to the well-known Dragon and Daemon battleships, all known Lucifers feature extensive hull scarring that implies they have a long service record and are therefore not newly-constructed. Why they are being deployed against humanity now is a question that has vexed the United Colonies of Mankind, and which does not bode well for the future.

The Lucifer is on the more supportive end of these "new" Scourge battleships, featuring relatively light weaponry despite its class. Instead, the Lucifer is optimized for speed, allowing it to pounce on mispositioned enemy assets and make the most of its available firepower. This is aided by its extensive launch bays, which it can almost always be in position to deploy where they're needed.

The Devil is a class of battleship designed and constructed by the Scourge. Alongside Beelzebub- and Lucifer-class battleships, Devil-class vessels have materialized over contested war zones throughout the Reconquest, seemingly from nowhere. As these ships are all of similar age to existing classes, the implication is that these are not new - leading to the more concerning question of why the Scourge did not see fit to deploy them against humanity until now.

The Devil shares the underslung mega plasma lance battery with the Beelzebub-class, but from there the two classes differ. Where the latter mounts banks of furnace cannons, the former instead features rack upon rack of voidcraft, allowing it to swarm the opposition with bombers at a moment's notice or throw up massive fighter screens.

The Beelzebub is a class of battleship designed and constructed by the Scourge. Much to the concern of the UCM's Office of Naval Intelligence, the Beelzebub - alongside several other never-before-seen classes of Scourge battleship - have begun to appear on the battlefields of the Reconquest. As with the previously-encountered classes, the hulls of these ships are scarred and pitted from countless years of service. Why these classes are only being committed now is a question of great concern for the UCM and its allies.

The Beelzebub differentiates itself from its contemporaries thanks to its furnace batteries - two collections of furnace cannons that can output enough firepower to melt through cruisers in a single salvo. As if that wasn't enough, the Beelzebub also packs an underslung mega plasma lance battery on a traversable mount to give it an edge against enemy battleships, as well as potent close action (as is the standard for Scourge vessels).

The Dragon is a class of battleship designed and constructed by the Scourge. As with its sister class, the Daemon, the Dragon is one of the oldest classes of warship still in service with the Scourge, and similarly is assumed to no longer be in production. Though some optimistic naval planners have postulated that the Scourge have lost the capacity to build more battleships, it's equally possible that the Scourge have simply shifted resources to building larger ships, such as their dreadnoughts.

Though the Dragon's anti-ship armament is comparatively small, the class makes up for this with two cavernous hangars and a pair of Scourge torpedoes, giving it significantly more flexibility than its counterpart battleship. As a result, Dragons are generally found in the center of Scourge vanguard fleets, the better to support their allies or clear a path through their enemies.

The Daemon is a class of battleship designed and constructed by the Scourge. Like its sister class, the Dragon, the Daemon is one of the oldest starship designs still in service with the Scourge, behind only the rarely-seen super-dreadnoughts.

Based on the general aging and battle scars sighted on these battleships, the UCM's naval planners estimate they were constructed somewhere between 500 to 2000 years ago, making them truly ancient.

Newer Daemons have never been sighted, leading some to speculate that the Scourge have lost the ability to construct new ones. Regardless of whether or not it's true, the Scourge have yet to replace any destroyed battleships and only deploy those they have at their disposal when the outcome is assured.

Regardless of age, the Daemon possesses firepower beyond question. Its prow is laced with oculus weaponry and tipped with a pair of furnace fangs, making it one of the most potent vessels available to the Scourge.

ship.lore: The Umbra is unusual for a Scourge warship in that it helps other vessels do the killing. A fast battlecruiser, the class is built around a crest-like precision targeting and target-painting device known simply as the “Oculus Booster”. As the name suggests, this heightens the threat level of Scourge Oculus weapons by pre-heating the target at weak points, providing a softened point of impact. Even a pre-heat of a few hundred degrees critically accelerates the Oculus weapon’s energy discharge on impact. At close range the effect is akin to plunging a hot steel rod into warm cheese. Hive-like cooperation is often observed among Scourge forces - this class exemplifies that. As part of a spear tip of Oculus-equipped warships, an Umbra should be considered the priority-1 target and only becomes more dangerous when accompanying the largest ships.

ship.lore: The Shadow is one of the Scourge’s most dangerous close action killers, and that’s saying something. Unlike its subtle cousin the Banshee, the Shadow has no cloaking technology due to the conspicuous energy signature of its main weapon: the Magnetron Lash. This horror discharges wild, sustained arcs of highly energetic particles which latch on to areas of high density. Heavy armour is especially prone to attracting and holding an arc. Once latched on, the temperature at the impact site nears that of a main sequence star. The hole it makes in the target is small, but antimatter bomblets are then passed down the beam into the target, which annihilate with the hull. With no cloak and primarily close-action weapons, Shadows normally approach on silent running, revealing themselves to a large, heavy target at the last moment. Once its weapons are blazing, a swift kill usually follows - fortunate since the class cannot fight and manoeuvre without attracting vengeful return fire.

ship.lore: The Basilisk is likely one of the oldest types of Scourge cruiser-based ships in service with the enemy. During the original Scourge invasion, they were feared above all other threats due to their combination of speed, heavy firepower and ability to mask their own energy spikes. The last attribute is the most crucial, enabled by its massive cloaking crest - the most effective of its kind in the Scourge navy. These qualities made the class the preeminent cause of civilian shipping loss, mostly unfortunate souls fleeing the carnage or poorly defended supply vessels, annihilated far too quickly for any response. This mission profile was highly effective and possibly an inspiration for the UCMF’s battlecruiser program. Recently, examples of the Basilisk are increasingly rare, replaced by a new and equally deadly type known as the Akuma. This class has been recently favoured by Scourge shipwrights over the older design. Most likely, it is simply more efficient to produce and operate, incorporating advancements the aliens have made in recent centuries.

ship.name: Kulshedra Heavy Carrier
ship.lore: The Kulshedra was first seen by the UCM during the Scourge’s assault on Ferrum. Reports state middling combat performance at range, but the Scourge’s reckless tactics never left it at range for long. Designated the moniker Vilestars, Kulshedra’s would dive straight into cruiser formations and take out lead ships before disgorging waves of fighters and bombers. While not an effective tactic for the longevity of the Kulshedra, its effect on UCM morale and formations was undeniable. More valuable Scourge ships were left alone while panicked UCM crews focused on the Kulshedra. Analysis of wrecks suggest that these ships are as old as the ones that assaulted the Cradle Worlds so long ago. Their seeming absence may speak of Scourge battle tactics. Rather than fight an unknown enemy, the Kulshedra is a weapon of distraction for enemies the Scourge know. It was undeniably useful above Ferrum, where a battlegroup of three Kulshedra’s caused a massive break in UCM formations, causing the loss of several Battlegroups, as they were too busy dealing with the Kulshedras to fight back against the Scourge ships taking advantage of the distraction.

ship.lore: The Shenlong class heavy cruiser is a highly dangerous and nefarious foe in ship-ship combat due in part to its extensive array of oculus weapons but also to its stealth capabilities. Mounted on its distinctive crest, the vessel features a suite of systems designed to mask weapons fire while silent running and to limit the visibility of extreme actions to enemy scanners. This makes the Shenlong an excellent ambush predator as well as hunter of capital ships where it can use these advantages to get the first shot all while avoiding return fire. The only downside to these stealth systems is the volume of space they  take up aboard ship and the amount of energy they consume, leading the Shenlong to be somewhat under-gunned compared to its equivalents in other races’ navies. However, it is still more heavily armed than all standard cruisers and its first strike and fire avoidance capabilities more than compensates for this minor limitation, making the Shenlong one of the most feared vessels in the Scourge vanguard.

ship.lore: The Raiju class heavy cruiser follows a similar design principle to its cousin, the Shenlong. Most importantly, it includes the latter’s highly effective stealth systems. It varies from the Shenlong in that it is equipped with a more diverse set of armaments, giving it a different mission profile. Its extensive arsenal includes a pair of furnace cannons - deadly beam weapons with multiple fire modes, allowing the Raiju to slice at multiple parts of a ship simultaneously or focus on reducing a specific area to molten slag. Significantly, this destructive power can be leveraged while the ship is silent running, thanks to its stealth systems. The result is that Raijus tend to stay in silent running condition longer than Shenlongs, since the latter must unleash all its weapons to be truly dangerous. These factors make the Raiju a specialised hunter of specific ships, wielding the furnace cannons while remaining virtually invisible to enemy scanners. The ability of these weapons to heat an enemy vessel’s hull to the point that they become more visible to the Scourge’s own scanners is a force- multiplier, as the victim can be engaged more easily from range while the Raiju is denied to enemy return fire.

ship.name: Hydra Fleet Carrier
ship.lore: The Hydra class fleet carrier is a dedicated strike craft platform designed to attack distant targets and support friendly vessels. Its capacious hangars contain hundreds of lethal Hellmaw bombers and predatory Hellscream fighters, their pure Scourge crews held in a fugue state in row upon row of storage racks until they are ready to be set loose. The almost mindless aggression of these craft suggest a psychotic level of dedication to slaughter - perhaps deliberately induced on their crews by the cocktail of narcotics flowing through them while kept dormant aboard ship. As a carrier, the Hydra is a more focused design than its closest current equivalent in the UCMF, the Seattle class, as it boasts a higher launch capacity at the expense of conventional firepower. As such, Hydras are usually protected by escort vessels in combat and are most frequently seen towards to rear of Scourge formations where the vulnerable carrier can be best protected. In spite of this weakness, the Hydra is one of the most lethal vessels of cruiser tonnage in the entire Scourge navy - a flexible and deadly threat which demands responsive tactics from any opponent.

ship.name: Chimera Troopship
ship.lore: The Chimera class troopship is the primary means by which the majority of the Scourge infantry hordes attain planetfall. Its cavernous interior accommodates many thousands of Scourge warriors, Destroyers, Razorworms and many other biological horrors so feared by humanity. It delivers its deadly payload to the surface via bulk lander direct from low orbit, making it better suited to second wave operations when safe landing zone is more likely. Like most Scourge ships, the Chimera is faster than its human equivalents, giving it an edge in reaching uncontested ground first at the expense of Given the sheer scale of the vessel and its bulk landers, it can also accommodate and deploy some of the largest Scourge ground based assets such as defence batteries, helping to cement the aliens’ iron grip on captured territory. Destruction of Chimeras is always a high priority for any opposing force, such is the threat they pose to victory on the surface.

ship.name: Wyvern Cruiser
ship.lore: The Wyvern class is the standard assault-oriented cruiser in the Scourge navy. It is equipped with a formidable array of lethal close ranged plasma cannons in addition to the oculus beam weapons present on virtually every Scourge cruiser. The Wyvern is often seen at the heart of the most brutal engagements, taking on vulnerable targets with poor point defence such as frigates, allowing other Scourge assets to concentrate on the capital ships. Since it needs to be close to the enemy to inflict maximum damage, Wyverns frequently spend the opening stages of a battle in silent running mode, closing the distance with the target/s while not giving the enemy a chance to accurately lock on. Once in the fray, Wyverns are famously vicious and merciless, even at the expense of their own safety. While many Scourge vessels attain an apparently great age, Wyverns seldom survive beyond their first century.
ship.namesake: A wyvern, the two-legged winged dragon of European heraldry, fierce and venom-tailed.

ship.name: Sphinx Cruiser
ship.lore: The Sphinx is the most common vessel of cruiser tonnage in the Scourge navy.  Much like its smaller cousin the Harpy class frigate, this vessel is armed predominantly with oculus type beam weapons. These are mounted in several groups on the prow of the vessel, positioned to cover overlapping fire arcs giving the Sphinx flexible options on how to engage the enemy as well as the potential to attack multiple foes simultaneously. However, such an arrangement requires a target to be in the front quarter should its captain wish to unload all weapons on a single opponent. The Sphinx offers a good balance of flexibility, firepower and survivability (for a Scourge ship), explaining its popularity with whatever passes for command among the cursed aliens. It is theorised that this design was the originator of most modern Scourge cruisers, as many of the oldest (as estimated) cruisers witnessed belong to this class. This may however stem from their greater survival rate in battle than some of their cousins, such as the Wyvern.
ship.namesake: The Sphinx, the lion-bodied riddler of Greek myth who devoured any traveller that failed her riddle.

ship.name: Ifrit Cruiser
ship.lore: The Ifrit class cruiser is the most common wielder of the formidable furnace cannons, sustained beam weapons designed to slice through armour, hulls and core systems. A pair of these are mounted on the Ifrit’s prow and integrated into the hull, limiting its effectiveness to the front quarter but giving the ship consummate killing power. In addition to directing multiple beams at various weak points, the weapons can also be focused at a single area, greatly increasing its armour penetrating capabilities at the expense of more widespread damage. That second fire mode also has the added benefit of heating the victim’s hull to such an extent that its signature increases, aiding the rest of the fleet in targeting the by now damaged ship. This makes the Ifrit highly useful in specialised situations, where it can mark targets for other ships. This is particularly effective against larger vessels such as battleships, giving the Scourge a window to wreak devastation on them before they have a chance to return fire.
ship.namesake: An ifrit, a powerful and cunning fire-demon of Arabian myth, among the most fearsome classes of djinn.

ship.name: Yokai Light Cruiser

ship.lore: The Yokai class light cruiser carries an identical weapons loadout to the heavier Sphinx class cruiser. Unlike its cousin, it sacrifices point defence capabilities and hull superstructure for additional combat speed. With its large number of conventionally capable oculus beam weapons, it is a similarly talented ship-killer although given its limitations it is best employed far from enemy fleet carriers or missile frigates. It is most effective when hunting strategically important targets weaker than itself and away from the core of the battle, where it would quickly be overwhelmed by close action attacks. The Yokai’s speed and its full cruiser level firepower are its greatest assets and in many ways it can be thought of as an application of the battlecruiser principle on a smaller scale. Outside of fleet engagements, this class is one of the most feared by support vessel crews, as it is frequently employed away from Scourge lines. There it can harass the enemy’s supply chain, unleashing its deadly weapons from range and swiftly disappearing before reprisals can be brought to bear.
ship.namesake: Yokai, the vast family of supernatural creatures and spirits of Japanese folklore.

ship.name: Strix Light Cruiser

specialRules.name: Vanguard-6"
specialRules.description: Groups with this rule may begin the game Directly Deployed, ignoring the normal Scenario Deployment and Approach Types (though still counting towards Groups Directly Deployed). If it does, it may be deployed up to 6” away from your Deployment Zone.

ship.lore: The Strix class light cruiser is perhaps the most aggressive capital ship type in the entire Scourge navy. Its design is focused entirely on speed and high powered close action capability in the form of a potent array of plasma cannons. It is a consummate decapitation vessel, adept at hunting and destroying key targets in the early stages of an engagement. However, when compared to its full cruiser cousin the Wyvern, the Strix has very poor point defence capability and reduced hull, making it highly vulnerable to return fire. Due to this fragility, Strix class light cruisers are usually employed on the flanks of the Scourge line where they may hope to utilise silent running tactics and peripheral involvement to avoid the worst of enemy reprisals. In addition, they usually operate in concert with other ships of the class, granting safety in numbers and further magnifying their destructive potential as they may combine fire to overload the point defences of any target with their potent close action weaponry.
ship.namesake: A strix, the screech-owl of Roman myth believed to feed by night on the flesh and blood of the unwary.

ship.name: Gremlin Light Cruiser

specialRules.name: Vanguard-6"

ship.lore: The Solar variants seen use the more common battle tactics the Scourge usually employ for their Light Cruisers, hunting in packs and flanking their targets, ready to sink their teeth into fresh prey.
ship.namesake: A mischievous gremlin, the imp blamed by airmen for unexplained mechanical faults and sabotage.

ship.lore: Thankfully, this vessel’s main weapon is unique to it. The Anharmonic Resonator is marked by two distinctive emanation banks along the ship’s midsection and is one of the most despised weapons any captain might face, hence the moniker given to whatever captain this ship has: The Hated. This individual throws its ship into combat with little regard for personal safely, unfortunate, since the weapon’s effects are limited to close victims. The Resonator throws pulsing waves of penetrating subatomic particles and exotic radiations into the target, causing a range of unpredictable internal effects, crew deaths, widespread vomiting, and systems failures. Given the necessity of being near the target, Little Chaos is equipped with one of the best stealth suites yet observed on any Scourge vessel. It is speculated that this ship was exceedingly difficult for the enemy to build or is challenging to maintain since they have produced no other known examples despite its horrible effectiveness. There are even suggestions that its entire crew might die of radiation poisoning after an engagement, although the captain’s consistent behaviour suggests that it, at least, fights from a heavily shielded bridge.
ship.namesake: [Chaos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_(cosmogony)) was the primordial void in Greek cosmogony, the formless gap that existed before all else. In Hesiod's Theogony it is the first being to come into existence, from which Erebus and Nyx were born.

ship.name: Revenant Destroyer

specialRules.name: Stealth
specialRules.description: This Ship may fire one Weapon while Silent Running.

ship.lore: The Revenant is one of the most feared of the Scourge destroyers, and for good reason. The class offers a range of options for dealing death, from conventional Oculus weapons, to powerful close action, to bomber capacity. In particular, this combination allows the ship to unleash its full destructive potential subtlety, without having to generate significant energy spikes all while still able to manoeuvre. This varied armament and ability makes it a consistently deadly foe, especially for groups of frigates at close range. The downside to this mixed approach is that its capacity for fighters and bombers is proportionately low, explaining its designation as a destroyer as opposed to an escort carrier by the Admiralty. In order to build up significant waves of bombers able to overcome enemy point defence, Revenants frequently hunt in larger packs than typical Scourge destroyers. A full group of four of these accomplished killers is a threat to almost anything in the battlespace.
ship.rulesText: This ship may take a Cloaking Crest for +5 pts, gaining Cloak-2 and Stealth.
famousShips: The Four Horsemen (group of four vessels)
ship.namesake: A revenant, a corpse risen from the grave in medieval folklore to torment the living.

ship.name: Succubus Destroyer

specialRules.name: Stealth
specialRules.description: This Ship may fire one Weapon while Silent Running.

ship.lore: The Succubus is the most common Scourge vessel of destroyer tonnage encountered in the Reconquest so far. Although they are far less common than frigates, the enemy appears to be increasing its use of destroyers, especially where increasingly outnumbered. Such ships are useful in that they offer the speed and utility of a frigate with increased resilience and firepower. As a fighting ship, the Succubus has proven to be highly adaptable and capable. It is a troublesome opponent for capital ships and swarms of lighter vessels alike due to its numerous weapons systems. The only downside to this armament is its power consumption, producing highly conspicuous energy spikes when fully unleashed. This is often mitigated by the inclusion of a cloaking crest, similar to that employed by larger Scourge vessels. It appears that this is an optional addition that is not always present in the class. Naval analysts have speculated that such technology is resource intensive, and only sees use where the enemy needs it most.
ship.rulesText: This ship may take a Cloaking Crest for +5 pts, gaining Cloak-2 and Stealth.
ship.namesake: A succubus, a female demon of European folklore that visits and drains sleeping men.

ship.name: Incubus Destroyer

specialRules.name: Stealth
specialRules.description: This Ship may fire one Weapon while Silent Running.

ship.lore: The Incubus is the sister class of the more common Succubus. It carries a more conspicuous armament; a single enlarged furnace cannon, a fearsome weapon capable of cutting to the heart of any adversary. The weapon also offers multiple fire modes, as it does on larger Scourge ships, making it useful for damage dealing and target marking. The latter mode is especially potent in this class, as a pack of these ships can heat an enemy vessel’s hull to extreme levels, making it highly visible to the rest of the fleet. Coupled with an optional cloaking crest, the Incubus is an excellent expeditionary The class also features formidable close action weaponry far superior to that of most Scourge frigates and equivalent to other destroyers. This makes the Incubus a multi-role threat that should always be considered in any battle plan. Failure to deal with these ships in the early stages of an engagement risks losing the advantage at longer ranges usually expected when facing the Scourge.

ship.namesake: An incubus, a demon of European folklore that preys upon sleepers in the dead of night.

specialRules.name: Vectored

specialRules.name: Energy Siphon
specialRules.description:
Before or after this Group completes any step in its activation, you may have it siphon energy. If you do, pick one other Group within 3” without the Energy Siphon special rule. That Group loses all Spikes and this Group gains those Spikes.
After siphoning at least one Spike from another Group, increase the Attack of this Group’s Siphoned Oculus Rays by 1 until the end of the round. If this Group has 3 or more Spikes after siphoning, increase the Attack of this Group’s Siphoned Oculus Rays by 2 until the end of the round instead.
When this Group is on the General Quarters or Silent Running Orders, it gains Regenerate-X, where X is the amount of Spikes it removes at the start of its activation.

ship.lore:
Remaining stealthy on approach to the kill is one of the central tenets of Scourge naval combat, given the lethality of their close range weapons; the Parasite is an unusual vessel which assists in this. Through the use of its siphon, Parasites can drain excess hull energy from other ships and take it into themselves. The Parasite can then redirect this energy to overcharge its Oculus weapons to cruiser-level destructive potential. Most effective in packs, Parasites can also locally share this acquired energy, meaning only one ship at a time need expose itself with a dangerously high resultant signature.

As a cutter-type vessel the Parasite is also extremely fast, allowing it to keep pace with any friendlies and to close with the enemy to disgorge its scalding plasma.

In an overtly offensive role, excess energy can even be siphoned from enemy vessels, normally in dense, close combat where energy signatures are less tactically relevant.

ship.lore: The Wraith is the archetypal cutter: a small, fast hunter of already fast enemy scouts, outliers and support vessels. Since speed is a typical asset of the Scourge, their cutters are among the fastest ships ever encountered by mankind. Currently, nothing the UCMF possesses can outrun a Wraith. They are feared by rearguard vessels such as the Lima, but especially by supply convoys and merchantmen, who frequently fall prey to roving packs of Wraiths far from recorded Scourge presence. Their very existence ensures no known space is 100% safe from enemy action. In combat, the Wraith can strike at range with conventional Oculus Rays, but from an easily-achieved close position a variant of this directed energy technology can scorch the hulls of any target, regardless of their point defences.
ship.namesake: A wraith, a ghostly apparition of Scottish lore whose appearance often heralds a death.

ship.name: Apsasu Barge
ship.namesake: [Apsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abzu), also spelled Abzu, was the Mesopotamian personification of the primordial freshwater ocean believed to lie beneath the earth. In the Babylonian creation epic Enuma Elish he is the consort of the saltwater goddess Tiamat and a source of all creation.

ship.name: Lamassu Barge
ship.lore: The Lamassu is little threat to attackers from without, but rather to invaders below. They are the smallest Scourge ships to carry bulk landers and are thought of as mobile, orbital barracks. During an invasion a Lamassu can drop thousands of troops whenever called upon. In many ways, this is more effective than re-routing troops already on the ground. Unlike Strike Carriers, they are not suited to a first strike role, given the vulnerability of bulk landers to ground fire and their slow speed. In order to support its charges, the Lamassu also features limited orbital bombardment capability, allowing it to soften up any landing zone that does have defences in place. During the Battle for Earth, orbital fire and incoming reinforcements from these otherwise innocuous small ships caught some UCM generals fatally unprepared.
ship.namesake: An Assyrian guardian spirit, a colossal winged bull with a human head, set at palace gates to repel evil.

ship.name: Shedu Monitor

If it does, at the end of its activation place two Spikes on an enemy Group in line of sight. A Group that uses Detector gains a Spike (regardless of the amount of Ships using this rule).

ship.lore: The Shedu class is actually a fairly typical monitor, offering the usual characteristics – low speed, high armour, high firepower. It lacks the ability to engage surface targets though, armed with a rare variant of Oculus weapon technology, designed for engaging targets in higher orbital layers. It also fulfils the useful secondary role of long-range scanning, lighting up targets for other ships.
ship.namesake: A Mesopotamian protective spirit, a winged bull-man set as a guardian upon the thresholds of palaces.

ship.lore: The Gargoyle class strike carrier is a first strike assault vessel which is capable of deploying clouds of lethal and outlandish Scourge dropships direct into atmosphere. It is typically employed in the first wave of a Scourge invasion or at the speartip of any counterstrike operations, where its nimble dropships with their deadly armoured payload can be expected to make it past most orbital defences to the heart of the dropzone. Unlike the UCM’s New Orleans class, the Gargoyle does not usually stay on station  to support its forces after the initial engagement. Instead, it withdraws to orbit where it can be resupplied with fresh dropships and ground troops, much like a regular ship would re-arm when out of ammunition. The distinctive silhouette of the Gargoyle is always a dreaded sight for beleaguered ground forces who know that very soon, hundreds of swift and lethal grav-tanks will be overwhelming their positions.
ship.namesake: The grotesque stone beast perched on medieval cathedrals to spout rainwater and, in legend, ward off evil.

ship.name: Scylla Frigate

specialRules.name: Descent
specialRules.description:
When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.
When attacking into Orbit from Atmosphere, any attack always hits on a 6+.
A non-Descent Ship that ends its activation in Atmosphere takes D3 damage. Colossal Ships take 2D3 damage instead.

ship.lore: The Scylla class frigate is an unusual vessel with an equally unorthodox armament and mission profile. Equipped with a set of reverse-grav cannons, these ships are designed to operate in atmosphere and fire up at enemy ships in orbit. This weapon is one of the very few effective at firing from atmosphere at orbital targets, although it does have the significant drawback of only working near gravity wells and only being able to engage targets in orbital layers above its own. The Scylla’s mode of attack is analogous to the missile submarines of 20th Century Earth, silent and hard to target submerged vessels designed to strike at surface targets. Since ships can only move relatively slowly due to air resistance in atmosphere, this ship’s task is usually defensive in nature. It can use its speed to reach its place of attack, but once ‘submerged’ in atmosphere it must wait for enemy ships to draw near. Since ships in atmosphere are usually so hard to target and destroy, this makes the Scylla an excellent deterrent or monitor ship, protecting Scourge territory from aggressors above.
ship.namesake: A six-headed Greek sea monster that plucked sailors from the cliffs, paired with the whirlpool Charybdis.

ship.name: Charybdis Frigate

specialRules.name: Descent
specialRules.description:
When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.
When attacking into Orbit from Atmosphere, any attack always hits on a 6+.
A non-Descent Ship that ends its activation in Atmosphere takes D3 damage. Colossal Ships take 2D3 damage instead.

ship.lore: The Charybdis class is an unusual ship as it is of frigate tonnage yet is the Scourge’s primary orbital bombardment platform. This differs greatly from other races which usually employ much larger ships for this task due to their ability to stay on station while soaking up enemy fire. Although the Charybdis cannot match its contemporaries in that regard, it can outpace them, allowing the Scourge to open bombardment very early in any engagement or to reach areas inaccessible in a short timeframe to more ponderous ships. It also gains a small measure of protection from its minimal signature, forcing the enemy to close the distance to obtain a firing solution, bringing them into the preferred killing range of other Scourge ships. What it lacks in size it makes up for in firepower, thanks to its potent plasma bombards, weapons rightly dreaded by all ground forces. These ensure that not even enemies in reinforced bunkers are safe as a single shot can reduce a city block to molten glass or shatter concrete bastions to powder.
ship.namesake: A monstrous Greek whirlpool that swallowed the sea three times a day, lurking opposite the man-eating Scylla.

ship.name: Djinn Frigate

specialRules.name: Descent
specialRules.description:
When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.

ship.lore: The Djinn class frigate is a fast, ultra aggressive vessel that perhaps best personifies the Scourge attitude to war. Its armament includes a much enhanced set of plasma weapons over regular Scourge frigates, giving it fantastic destructive power at close ranges for its size. This ship is far more effective when employed in very large squadrons, where massed plasma fire can overwhelm even a battleship’s point defence capabilities. In battle, the Djinn must use its superior speed and manoeuvrability to close the distance to the enemy. Silent running is a tactic frequently employed by these pack hunters, combining their small signature with low power output to screen them from enemy targeting systems until they are close enough to pounce. Alternatively, they can use their atmospheric flight capability to lie in wait for the enemy to come to them - a tactic which is sometimes enough to deter aggressors from approaching at all, thus holding ground without having to fire a shot or risk themselves to enemy reprisals.
ship.namesake: A djinn (genie), a spirit of smokeless fire in Arabian myth, able to grant wishes or work terrible harm.

ship.name: Harpy Frigate

specialRules.name: Descent
specialRules.description:
When attacking a City or a Descent Ship in Atmosphere, that attack always hits on a 6+ and can never cause a critical.
When attacking a non-Descent Ship in Atmosphere, reduce the lock of Weapons attacking it by 1.
When attacking into Orbit from Atmosphere, any attack always hits on a 6+.
A non-Descent Ship that ends its activation in Atmosphere takes D3 damage. Colossal Ships take 2D3 damage instead.

ship.lore: The Harpy is a class of frigate designed and constructed by the Scourge, and is the race's standard combat frigate. Harpies are by far the most common combat ship encountered by the UCM, with almost 600 believed to exist as of 2672. These small vessels are armed with potent oculus beam weaponry and generally operate in packs, relying on safety in numbers and weight of firepower to bring down heavier vessels. Unlike the frigates of other factions, Harpies are capable of operating in atmosphere, though their oculus beams are of limited value once ensconced there. Instead, they use this capability to hide from enemy sensors, waiting for the perfect moment to strike. Even if an enemy detects them in advance, the atmosphere itself can protect a Harpy from the worst of an enemy's void weaponry.
ship.namesake: A harpy, the winged woman-bird of Greek myth who snatched away food and souls upon storm winds.

ship.lore: The Hiruko brings all manner of bio-nightmares into personal, bloody contact in a way only the Scourge can. Almost uniquely, the Hiruko is designed specifically for ramming and more than that - to actually make physical contact with a target. Given the lethality of point-blank defence fire, this is always a one-way trip, so the Hiruko is equipped with a potent Plasma Torch and latching tentacles to quickly inject its savage payload into the bowels of the target. Beyond the rents torn by clashing tons of starship, it eventually spells doom for a ship of any size as its crew find their clean uniforms and shiny corridors painted crimson by the deadly boarding party - often made up of the most vicious close quarters Scourge hosts.
ship.namesake: Hiruko, the 'leech child' of Shinto myth, a malformed deity set adrift on the sea by its divine parents.

ship.name: Nickar Hunter-Killer

weapons.name: Plasma Squall
weapons.special: Air to Air, Close Action, Scald-2

ship.lore: The Nickar class hunter-killer is a small, atmospheric-capable vessel of sub-frigate tonnage. These nimble, fast ships are rightly feared by any enemy vessel that operates in atmosphere - this ship’s favourite hunting ground. Armed with specialist plasma munitions, these deadly predators can easily destroy vessels larger than themselves such as strike carriers. In the opening days of the Reconquest, this class was responsible for more Armoured Corps losses than ground actions. Thousands of men and vehicles were lost to hunterkiller incursions aboard their strike carriers before they even made it to the surface. Since these vessels operate in the relative safety of atmosphere, the best measure against them is corvettes - a lesson learned the hard way by the Admiralty who no longer discount such small ships in their battle plans.
ship.namesake: A nicker (or nixie), a shape-shifting water-spirit of Germanic folklore that lures travellers to drown.

ship.name: Pungari Thresher Hive Ship

specialRules.name: Subservient Mercenaries
specialRules.description: Pungari Threshers may be used in any fleet but always use Shaltari Fire Ships. When used in a Shaltari fleet, this Ship gains Shield-5+.

specialRules.name: Rare
specialRules.description: You may only take one Group of this Ship in a Skirmish-sized game, two in a Clash, three in a Battle, and four in a Reconquest.

ship.lore:
The UCM first encountered the Pungari as part of a Shaltari force during Phase 2 of the Reconquest. Unlike their masters, they were prolific in numbers. In them, the Shaltari found a subservient race to exploit in much the same way they had planned for humanity.

Sightings of Pungari ships were reported shortly afterwards, not all had fallen in with the Shaltari. Apparently, the Pungari are new to starfaring; their blocky ships are primitive yet robust. Instead of the low-crew, high-firepower approach advanced generators afford to other races, the Pungari leverage sheer numbers. Routinely, they hurl thousands into suicidal boarding actions; something Pungari do willingly and, as far as UCM soldiers can tell, with much glee. Their stocky frames may cope with the extreme g-forces involved, unencumbered by too much brain to damage.

When encountering Pungari it is always a coin toss on whether they attack or not. They may try to broker simple alliances, happy to plunge into the wars of other races without expecting much in return, beyond a master to serve in awe.

ship.name: Hyperyacht Aurorum

specialRules.name: Marines-2
specialRules.description: Remove 2 enemy Battalions from this Ship at the beginning of the Battalion Combat step.

ship.lore:
Hyperyacht Aurorum, launched 2493, was commissioned by Caesar Dun, boss of the East Eden Syndicate. She was uniquely built to impeccable standards, riddled with unregistered spaces, and armed far beyond EAA-sanctioned levels. While using her peerless stealth capabilities to evade justice, he unwittingly dodged the Scourge invasion. After months of shadowing a survivor flotilla, Caesar was garrotted by his lieutenant, who took Aurorum to join the refugees.

Today, Aurorum serves as the flagship of Karl Stieglitz, head of the galaxy's most infamous mercenaries: The Decapitators. This privateer flotilla earned dark renown during the Battle of Earth in the vanguard of the Vega Scrapfleet but is now a gun for hire. Stieglitz has already been approached by Kalium and, it is rumoured, the PHR. The UCM has yet to decide how to respond.

ship.name: Hyperyacht Somniferum

specialRules.name: Unique
specialRules.description: You may only take one Group of this Ship.

ship.lore:
The Hyperyacht Somniferum is not a sight civilized governments want to see on situation reports. Colloquially known as "the party bus", a spike in crime and illegal substances usually follows in its wake. Somniferum's current owner is the "Master of Ceremonies" Maeby Hy. The Somniferum is almost unrecognisable from its initial configuration as an Eden Aerospace Systems Luxury Liner. Lab explosions, combat damage, and ad-hoc refits have all added to it's hodge-podge appearance.

One of these many changes to the ship is the addition of a peculiar weapon system. While it has no official name, the crew and any who face it have dubbed it "Party Poppers". This weapon system fires armour piercing fragmenting flechettes that disperse airborne narcotics and electromagnetic interference into its target. Far too small and numerous to effectively track, this weapon is able to bypass the majority of a ship's point defences and deliver strikes straight to the hull.

The Somniferum is rarely seen over combat zones, preferring to stick to those planets that are safe enough for civilian travel. While able to defend itself against small time competitors, the ship isn't built for combat. More often than not, the Somniferum will make a hasty exit from a planet as soon as it detects any law enforcement on an intercept course.

ship.name: LKS Dredger

specialRules.name: Industrial Design
specialRules.description: Improve this Group’s Backup save by 2 when rolling to save hits due to Debris Fields.

ship.lore:
A relentless machine of industry, built to mulch, sift, and extract until its timer runs dry. It drills deep, rips apart rock, and spits out raw profit, indifferent to the hands that keep it running. No legacy, no ownership, just a contract ticking toward expiration. When time is up, it moves on, leaving its crew behind, waiting for the next company to stake its claim on the battered frame. Inside, the workers endure the constant grind, wedged between failing systems and the unyielding demand for productivity. Comfort is non-existent, maintenance is endless.

Equipped with a heavy duty drill and front mounted mining array, this vessel doesn't just extract minerals, it carves deep trenches into asteroid surfaces and space debris, kicking up clouds of pulverized rock and metallic sediment. A network of sediment filters and gravity sifting tanks separates valuable ore from dust before storing the processed materials in its cargo bays.

Prominently displayed on the ship's exterior, the countdown display isn't a warning, it's a fact. The contract will expire, and if it doesn't get topped up, the vessel moves on to whatever comes next. Passed from one mining company to the next, these hand me down workhorses run until their rental contracts dry up. Refurbished just enough to stay functional, they degrade with every transfer, patched, battered, barely space worthy, considered scrap with engines.

Upper management doesn't care about the ship, only the ore it pulls in before time runs out. The crew works under relentless pressure, knowing there's no guarantee of renewal.

When the timer hits zero, it's out of their hands. Either the contract gets extended, or the ship moves on.

Despite its size, the colossal vessel remains a world of tight corridors for its 190 crew members. Dust and grime clings to every surface, settling in forgotten corners and coating equipment in a fine greasy layer. Minimal comforts, constant maintenance, and the daily expectation that something will break.

ship.name: SLM-9 Resupply Hauler

stats.special: Vectored, Resupply and Rearm, Flawed Design

ship.lore:
A relic from the now liquidated Eden Void Logistics inc, the SLM-9 is a battle tested bulk logistics vessel, trusted for fleet replenishment in high risk environments. Though the company behind its design has since shuttered, the SLM-9 endures as a testament to their engineering prowess and affordability. Its metal cargo frame, hydraulic deployment arms and universal clamps ensure rapid, adaptable resupply of ordnance, fuel, and supplies anywhere. Rugged and inexpensive, the SLM-9 remains a reasonable choice for fleets needing a dependable workhorse at a fraction of the cost of newer models.

Unlike conventional Logistics Vessels that unload cargo gradually, the SLM-9 releases its entire payload in a single, controlled operation. Hydraulic deployment arms manoeuvre the entire cargo bed outward, allowing for structured and efficient transfer without manual unloading.

Built for adaptability, the SLM-9's pincer like grappling arms latch onto ships regardless of docking compatibility. Variable force actuators fine tune pressure, securing a stable hold without compromising hull integrity. Whether resupplying warships or assisting stranded vessels, its clamps ensure critical cargo transfer under any conditions.

The SLM-9's hydraulic deployment arms are its defining feature, but also its greatest liability. If compromised by enemy fire or mechanical failure, the vessel loses its ability to unload cargo entirely, rendering it useless. A damaged deployment system means supplies remain trapped onboard, preventing fleet resupply and turning the ship into dead weight. While reinforced plating offers some protection, direct hits can buckle the arms, leading to catastrophic failure.

Due to its critical vulnerability, the SLM-9 has begun to be phased out in favour of newer resupply haulers with reinforced unloading mechanisms and modular backup systems. The remaining SLM-9 units are considered outdated relics, still operational but increasingly rare.

Ships can only be tugged this way up to a maximum of 6” each round.

ship.lore:
The T-Type was once a common sight across many shipyards. Due to the size of many pre-war ships, a way of moving these gargantuan vessels out of drydock was needed. T-Types were devised to be the answer to this sizeable problem. The first batch of these floated out of the assembly lines prior to the first Pathfinder, ready and waiting to guide it to a safe launching point. Since then, countless multitudes of these ships have been constructed. Most serve their entire service life in the void, however some are refitted as lunar landers once their superstructure becomes unusable for its intended purpose.

Only a small amount of these were refit with foldspace drives, the majority were only designed to work around a single planet and its satellites. Those that were refit tend to be found in independent fleets, where they assist in swapping components on their larger vessels. T-Types are not built for any form of combat, though their internal bracing gives them a certain resilience, they are unable to weather any attack from dedicated combat ships.

Some T-Types have been converted to function similarly to mines, albeit with a much more personal weapon system. These have weaponised their towing ability, captains with a death wish will attach their tug to an enemy vessel and set their engines to full. When performed right, this can violently tear vessels in half, though at the cost of the tugboat and its crew.

When any number of enemy Battalions are removed due to Boarding Actions or Battalion Combat on a Space Station within 6” of this Ship, place a single friendly Battalion on this Ship. This Ship’s Boarding Pods and Drop Pods can only be used while it has friendly Battalions on it and each Boarding Pod or Drop Pod launched causes one friendly Battalion on this Ship to be removed.

ship.lore:
The DH-Type represents one of the Colonial Fleet's largest run of dedicated long-range prison ships, built around a standardized architecture of reinforced armour, multi-tier detention decks and automated security. Originally intended strictly for high-risk inmate transport and remote incarceration, wartime pressures pushed the class into broader operational roles.

Though designed with consistent core systems, such as compartmentalized containment blocks, automated defensive suites, ECM shielding, and a C.A.G.E emitter field. The ships grew increasingly variable due to differing missions, retrofits, and partial deactivations. Although uncommon, Individual DH-Type vessels gained their own notoriety, such as Iron Veil, Remnant Forge, Dreadhold and Bright Spire. The DH-Type ships illustrated the evolution through conversions into troop transports, logistics carriers, medical ships, and frontier support platforms, often retaining traces of their original penal infrastructure.

In modern service, L1-class hulls endure as adaptable, if austere, multi-role assets. Their durable construction, intimidating infrastructure, and legacy security systems continue to define their operational character, reflecting both the robustness of the original design and the fleet's ongoing need to repurpose coercive architecture for broader demands.

ship.lore:
M-Type Barges are the larger cousin of the L-Type. Produced at the same Tharsis Manufacturing shipyards over Mars, the M-Type was designed for corporate bulk shipping. Many and more of these were owned and operated by the enduring shipping companies of old Earth, each of them emblazoned with corporate livery. Designed and built after the L-Type, these ships feature much improved Foldspace drives as well as the latest innovations in structural bracing. Optimisations in production brought the build time on these freight behemoths down to only twice that of the L-Type.

Many of these were spared the events of the Scourge invasion, most would have been slowly moving between the colonies and the cradle worlds, far enough away to make emergency jumps to safety. The initial trade and logistics network of the UCM was built upon the backs of the M-Type, their reliability and availability gave the colonies enough trade stability to recover from the loss of the cradle worlds. M-Types are surprisingly rare in Resistance fleets, most of the captains of these ships were more interested in meeting deadlines and quotas than in doomsday predictions prior to the battle of Vega. Kalium is yet to be seen operating these ships, preferring the L-Type for combat resupply, though may potentially be using M-Types in more secure Kalium controlled systems.

Recent developments in prefabricated defensive structures have allowed a small number of these ships to carry deployable missile defence outposts in place of their normal cargo compliment. These outposts are designed to grant a foothold on a planet and supplement its missile halo while more permanent structures are built, re-purposed, or captured.

ship.lore: The Oblivion OBV64 Barge is a heavily armoured civilian vessel designed to transport extremely hazardous materials, unstable technology, failed reactors, and biohazards, too dangerous to store on planets. These ships travel discreetly between remote depots, derelict battlefields, and disposal zones. Crewed by an extensive team of highly trained specialists under strict quarantine and secrecy protocols, The Oblivion barge handles cargo that is often poorly understood or classified. Their role is to quietly remove dangerous discoveries and remnants from circulation before they can threaten the wider fleet, or attract unwanted attention.

ship.lore:
The Type-87 Terminus Harvester is a colossal reclamation vessel built to consume the unrepairable wreckage of war. Its monolithic maw engulfs chunks up to frigate tonnage, feeding them into vast crushing chambers where superheated hydraulic presses obliterate hull plating to slag. Two VX-22 Flensers detach from its hull, peeling derelicts apart and hauling scraps to their final destruction. Ancient, slow-moving, and relentless, it labours, stripping vessels down to raw material. Within its corroded halls, life is harsh. Dim corridors reek of burning metal as air filters struggle against decades of industrial smog.

The Type-87's wedge-like prow is battered and scarred, worn from decades of grinding through wreckage. Deep gouges and warped plating mark where debris crumpled beneath its relentless push, clearing the way for the behemoth behind.

A monolithic opening capable of engulfing entire frigates, feeding them into a crushing chamber spanning the volume of a megastructure. Inside, reinforced walls lined with titanic hydraulic presses grind vessels down in a superheated maelstrom of pulverized metal, reducing all to molten slag.

Equipped with two VX-22 Flensers, these small salvage vessels dock onto the Harvester's hull when idle but detach to roam wreckage fields. They Brutally peel derelicts apart piecemeal while hauling fragmented components to the crushing maw. Though technically separate, they operate as an extension of the Harvester, ensuring no usable scrap escapes consumption.

stats.special: Payload F-1, Vectored, Scrap Collection, Unload, Industrial Design

specialRules.name: Payload F-1
specialRules.description:
When building your fleet, you may choose as many Payload Ships as you like— tonnage limits do not apply to these Ships, and they have no Group size. All Payload S/L Ships must be assigned to a Porter S/L Ship with the same letter. Payload Ships may not activate or be targeted until detached.
Payload Ships take up 1 of a Porter Ship’s capacity.
During the Porter Ship’s activation, if it is on an Order that allows it to Launch, you may detach one or more of its Payload Ships and place them within 3” of it. In the round they are detached, these Payloads activate together immediately as part of the Porter Ship’s activation after it has completed its Order. In subsequent rounds, all your Payload Ships count as being part of a single Group. Crippling Effects, Spikes, and other rules that affect an entire Group only affect the targeted Payload Ship.
Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.
If a Payload Ship is attached to a Porter Ship when that Ship is destroyed, the Payload Ship is destroyed.

ship.lore:
The VX-22 Flensers are compact salvage vessels designed for brutal ship dismantling. Their prow mounted sawblades don't cut cleanly, they tear, shred, and rip through wreckage with unrestrained violence. Designed for aggressive reclamation, they are the smaller, more aggressive sibling to the T-Type Tugboat. Where the Tugboat manoeuvres and stabilizes wreckage for controlled processing, the Flensers gut derelicts with reckless brutality, prioritizing destruction over precision.

Heavy rotating saws brutally cut through hull plating, breaking it into manageable pieces and scattering debris as they progress. Instead of delicate incision, the Flensers' sawblades operate at maximum torque, chewing through reinforced bulkheads with enough force to buckle surrounding structure.

Their cutting mechanisms frequently overheat, causing violent energy surges that make their hulls shudder mid operation.

The Flenser hurls debris into the Type-87 Terminus Harvester's compactor bay, sometimes suffering brutal kickback as the churning machinery spits chunks back out. When it happens, the debris slams into its failing frame, worsening the damage and making every load a gamble.

Positioned below the cockpit, this reinforced plating shields pilots from wreckage kicked up during cutting operations. Sloped for maximum deflection, it redirects debris that could slam into the hull with deadly force, absorbing impacts before they buckle metal or breach compartments.

ship.name: PRK-91 Provenance Ark
ship.lore:
A monolithic vessel of unimaginable scale, the Provenance Ark dwarfs most ships. A precursor to the modular construction found on Coloniser class vessels, these ships were a talisman of hope and expansionism. These are the first major terraforming vessels built by mankind, reaching out into an unknown universe. Built to prepare entire worlds for habitation, it carries vast stores of genetic material, atmospheric stabilizers, and autonomous resource systems. The Ark monitors planetary progress through an extensive network of sensors and automated regulators, adjusting atmospheric composition, maintaining microbial balance, and even modulating gravitational and magnetic fields to stabilize emerging terrains.

Entire cities once mere schematics, rise, with power grids, transport arteries, and habitation modules ready long before the first settlers arrive. Inside, Construction drones and biotic cultivators orchestrate the birth of forests, oceans, and breathable atmospheres with the precision of a master artisan.

Many ships of this class feature underslung terraforming torpedo launchers. While near useless in ship to ship combat, these torpedoes are geared towards atmospheric re-entry and contain a plethora of mutagens and nerve agents, some of which would be used on Senator class battlecruisers. Under normal circumstances the use of these would constitute a war crime. Here they are simply used to rid prospective landing areas of their megafauna, causing mass hysteria and aggression in local fauna. Any issues with unruly creatures take care of themselves, and those left over can be cut down by specialised anti-fauna vehicles. Once the LZ is cleared of hostiles, the terraformer can then deploy more traditional terraforming methods.

spaceStations.name: Ephyra
spaceStations.namesake: An ephyra is the free-swimming larval stage of a scyphozoan jellyfish, which later matures into the bell-shaped adult medusa. The term is borrowed from [Ephyra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephyra_(mythology)), an Oceanid water-nymph of Greek myth, a daughter of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys.

spaceStations.name: Nematocyst
spaceStations.namesake: A [nematocyst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cnidocyte) is the venomous stinging organelle housed within the cnidocyte cells of jellyfish, sea anemones, and other cnidarians. It fires a coiled, barbed thread to inject toxin into prey, in one of the fastest mechanical processes in nature.
